title: Kissing number in dimension 22, lower bound
statement: Find as many nonzero vectors as possible in R^22 with pairwise angles of at least 60 degrees; k such vectors show that the kissing number in dimension 22 is at least k. The best known configuration, by J. Leech (1967), has 49896 vectors; one with more vectors improves it. The upper bound is 80810 (Leijenhorst and de Laat).
submission: Text file: one vector per line, integer coordinates separated by spaces or commas, all with the same squared norm N; more than 22 coordinates are allowed when the vectors span a space of dimension at most 22. Every inner product between two vectors must be at most N/2. With 49,896 vectors or more the check is long (hours) in pure Python.
score: k, the number of vectors (larger is better)

best_known.source: kissing number in dimension 22 >= 49896: J. Leech (1967), in Henry Cohn's table of kissing numbers (cohn.mit.edu/kissing-numbers); read 9 Nov 2026

bound.source: N. Leijenhorst and D. de Laat (2022), in Henry Cohn's table
